ui_bugs.issue: Default label for a new alarm shows 'Morning Tithi' instead of 'सुबह की तिथि' when the app is in Hindi mode. Root cause: `const [label, setLabel] = useState(() => t('defaultLabel'))` on line 55 captures the translation during the first render, which happens before SettingsProvider hydrates lang='hi' from storage. The surrounding UI (title 'नया अलार्म', weekday buttons, sound labels, save button) is correctly Hindi, confirming context is loaded by paint time – only the label state is stuck on the initial English snapshot. Fix: derive the label from `t()` reactively (e.g. useEffect that resets label when lang changes and the field is untouched, or compute the placeholder/initial value with `useMemo` keyed on lang, or use the current lang directly when the component mounts after the Settings context is ready). Reference: /app/frontend/app/alarm-setup.tsx:55

integration_issues.issue: After tapping save-alarm-button on /alarm-setup opened via deep link, the app logs 'The action GO_BACK was not handled by any navigator' and never returns to home-screen (Expo Router has no history when the page is loaded directly). Not blocking in the real app flow (user enters via the FAB), but will bite anyone who deep-links or uses the back-button after a direct save. Consider `router.replace('/')` instead of `router.back()` after save. Reference: alarm-setup.tsx save handler.

action_items: alarm-setup.tsx:55 — make the default label reactive to the current language so Hindi mode shows 'सुबह की तिथि' instead of 'Morning Tithi' on a fresh alarm.

Replace `router.back()` after save/cancel on alarm-setup (and settings) with `router.replace('/')` (or guard with `router.canGoBack()`) so direct deep-link flows don't trigger the GO_BACK warning on web.
critical_code_review_comments: src/i18n.ts stores a long static map in module scope; fine today but if more locales get added, consider a lazy loader to keep bundle lean.

settings-context.tsx: the language choice is persisted but there is no migration path if the stored shape ever changes — add a schema version field alongside eveningEnabled/eveningHour/eveningMinute so you can safely evolve settings later.

server.py Hindi dictionaries (NAKSHATRA_HI, YOGA_HI, FESTIVAL_HI, OBSERVANCE_HI, SIGNIFICANCE_HI) silently fall back to the English string when a key is missing — add a backend unit test or log line so missing translations are discoverable instead of silently reaching the UI.
add_hindi() mutates the dict in-place and also returns it; pick one convention to avoid confusion for callers (especially where it's chained inside build_day).

rca_of_issue: Alarm-setup default label bug: useState initializer `() => t('defaultLabel')` runs during the first render of alarm-setup. SettingsProvider loads lang from AsyncStorage asynchronously; even though its state is updated before paint in most cases, the initializer still captures whatever `t()` returned at that first synchronous render (English default). Subsequent re-renders see the updated lang, but `label` state is already fixed — it only changes when the user types. Fix with either (a) `useEffect(() => { if (!dirty) setLabel(t('defaultLabel')); }, [lang])`, or (b) read placeholder from `t('labelPlaceholder')` and keep the stored value empty until user types, or (c) wait for `settingsReady` from the context before mounting the form.
